bands.label: Second term reset
bands.summary: Trump returns to office and reworks the China file around direct leader-to-leader dealings, tariff bargaining and a softer public vocabulary toward Beijing, Moscow and Pyongyang.

bands.label: Strategic competition era
bands.summary: Section 301 tariffs, tech export controls, the Phase One deal and Biden-era chip restrictions lock in a bipartisan framing of China as the central long-term competitor.

bands.label: WTO integration
bands.summary: China joins the WTO and is treated by successive US administrations as a rising stakeholder to be engaged, even as trade imbalances, South China Sea moves and Xi's consolidation steadily harden the mood in Washington.

bands.label: Opening and normalization
bands.summary: From Nixon's visit through full diplomatic recognition, MFN battles and the post-Tiananmen recalibration, Washington and Beijing build the engagement architecture that every later frame argues over.

frames.label: Jan 2025 second term
frames.note: The story begins when Trump returns to office and starts describing Beijing as a co-equal great power rather than a rival to be contained. Under this opening, the current G7 friction, NATO spending demands and outreach to Pyongyang read as one continuous reset built around that reframe. This is the frame Trump-aligned outlets and the White House itself open with.

frames.label: 2018 tariff round
frames.note: The story begins with the Section 301 tariffs and the formal turn to strategic competition with China. Under this opening, today's peer-power language is the latest move inside an eight-year confrontation that the first Trump term started and Biden largely kept. This is the frame China hawks, US trade officials and most Taipei-based coverage open with.

frames.label: 1972 Nixon opening
frames.note: The story begins with Nixon's trip to Beijing and the long bet that engagement would shape Chinese behavior. Under this opening, the current reframing is one more swing in a fifty-year cycle of opening, integration and pullback between two powers that have always managed each other as peers in practice. This is the frame realist historians, Russian and Chinese state outlets and many European analysts open with.
